All four successful pathway-analysis tools agree on a single dominant theme: the Leloir pathway and its connected sugar biology. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranked Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) as the top two hits with FDR 1.06×10⁻¹³, driven by five input metabolites (sucrose, myo-inositol, glycerol, galactinol, galactitol). Glycerol and myo-inositol additionally support the Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP:WP2533, FDR 3.3×10⁻⁴), linking sugar metabolism to membrane lipid remodelling. react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolite set shows overwhelming cross-paradigm consensus on disruption of galactose metabolism. All four successful pathway-analysis tools agree on a single dominant theme: the Leloir pathway and its connected sugar biology. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranked Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) as the top two hits with FDR 1.06×10⁻¹³, driven by five input metabolites (sucrose, myo-inositol, glycerol, galactinol, galactitol). MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed this with KEGG:hsa00052 ranked first at p=5.16×10⁻⁸. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently returned galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism) at rank 4 (p=0.0078). Together these three paradigms — RaMP ORA, MetaboAnalystR ORA, and Mummichog network-activity — converge on the same pathway with five shared driver metabolites. Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) and acetaminophen (paracetamol) independently hit the Aspirin ADME Reactome pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9749641, FDR 1.8×10⁻⁴) and the Synthesis of Prostaglandins Reactome pathway (REACT:R-HSA-2162123, FDR 2.9×10⁻⁴), reflecting their shared cyclooxygenase-target pharmacology. Glycerol and myo-inositol additionally support the Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP:WP2533, FDR 3.3×10⁻⁴), linking sugar metabolism to membrane lipid remodelling. The biological story is a coordinated carbohydrate and lipid response, anchored by galactose metabolism perturbations with drug-metabolism side-signals.

final_claims.claim_text: RaMP multi-DB ORA ranked SMPDB:SMP00043 (Galactose Metabolism) and KEGG:map00052 (Galactose Metabolism) jointly at ranks 1-2 with FDR 1.06×10⁻¹³.
MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism) first with p=5.16×10⁻⁸.
Mummichog m/z-network analysis ranked MUMM:galactose_metabolism fifth with p=0.00798.
Sucrose (KEGG:C00089) is a member of KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism).
myo-Inositol (KEGG:C00137) is a member of KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism).
Glycerol (KEGG:C00116) is a member of KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism).
Galactinol (KEGG:C01235) is a member of KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism).
Galactitol (KEGG:C01697) is a member of KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism).

The five-driver carbohydrate cluster for KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism) consists of sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), and galactitol (KEGG:C01697).
RaMP ranked KEGG:hsa00500 (Starch and Sucrose Metabolism) fourth with FDR 1.19×10⁻⁵.
Mummichog ranked MUMM:starch_and_sucrose_metabolism fourth with p=0.00672.
Reactome R-HSA-9749641 (Aspirin ADME) was enriched with FDR 1.82×10⁻⁴, hit by acetaminophen and aspirin.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranked SMPDB:SMP00043 (Galactose Metabolism) and KEGG:map00052 (Galactose Metabolism) jointly at ranks 1-2 with FDR 1.06×10⁻¹³, driven by five shared metabolites: sucrose, myo-inositol, glycerol, galactinol, and galactitol. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed the same pathway at KEGG:hsa00052 as its top hit with p=5.16×10⁻⁸, with the identical five metabolites. Mummichog m/z-network analysis ranked MUMM:galactose_metabolism fifth with p=0.00798, with 12 overlapping metabolites including the five-driver set. Starch and Sucrose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00500) emerged as a secondary signal: RaMP ranked it fourth with FDR 1.19×10⁻⁵ for sucrose, myo-inositol, glycerol, and ureidosuccinic acid, while mummichog independently ranked MUMM:starch_and_sucrose_metabolism fourth with p=0.00672. Aspirin and acetaminophen together enriched the Reactome R-HSA-9749641 (Aspirin ADME) pathway with FDR 1.82×10⁻⁴, consistent with their co-administration in the treatment group. Ureidosuccinic acid appeared in the broad Biochemical pathways super-pathway (WP:WP3604) at FDR 1.19×10⁻⁵ and in Pyrimidine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00240) with p=0.18, indicating no pathway-level significance for pyrimidine metabolism.
